speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in respect of the Workfare Special Payment (a) what is the rationale behind having up-to-date MediSave contributions as a qualifying criteria for the payment; (b) how many low-wage workers who are otherwise eligible for this payment have been prevented from receiving this due to arrears in their MediSave contributions; (c) how many of those who are not eligible for this payment have contribution arrears amounting to more than $3,000; and (d) whether the Ministry will consider removing such contributions as an eligibility criteria especially in this difficult time when liquidity and cashflow is needed by individuals to survive day to day.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For employees, the CPF contributions are made on a monthly basis by their employers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For Self-Employed Persons or SEPs, they will only need to make MediSave contributions at the end of the Work Year after declaring their incomes and this is the cause of MediSave arrears.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We recognise that this is a difficult period for many Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: But it is important for SEPs to continue saving for their healthcare needs through MediSave, while they also get support from the Government through Workfare.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The CPF Board has helped SEPs who faced difficulties by working out alternative arrangements for them to meet their MediSave obligations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Many lower income SEPs would also have received support under various Government schemes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Those facing difficult circumstances can also visit the MSF Social Service Offices if they need further help.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: While I understand the importance of CPF and MediSave, and the important role those play in ensuring long-term security for our workers in terms of their retirement and healthcare needs, would the Minister not agree that for individuals already facing cashflow difficulty in the current period, expecting them to make their MediSave arrears first before allowing them to get this payout to meet their immediate needs, is in fact defeating the purpose of the scheme in alleviating immediate financial challenges faced by these individuals?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This is in allusion to my maiden speech where I mentioned the good intentions of the Government to 雪中送炭变成雪上加霜.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, in view of that, will the Minister agree that we can allow these individuals to work out an instalment payment arrangement for their MediSave arrears, while at the same time making them eligible to receive the Workfare Special Payment?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am sure many Members have shared similar concerns and you would have seen residents who have similar difficulties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I would encourage everyone to look at this particular requirement, not in isolation but to look at the full suite of help measures that the Government has put in place.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Yes, there is Workfare Special Payment which is tied to the underlying Workfare requirement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But there are also many other help schemes in the Budget, through ComCare, through SIRS, through GST Voucher, where the help is provided more immediately and are not tied to any CPF contributions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I had mentioned earlier, the CPF Board is already doing its part to reach out to them and provide instalment plans to help these SEPs fulfil their MediSave obligations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am just wondering if the Minister can clarify for us whether in this particular period, there has been an increase in the subsidy payouts on the part of Workfare for citizens, in part because, obviously, due to COVID, some of these services may have actually seen reductions in their demand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, I am wondering if he could clarify for us.
